To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the teaching and learning process of research ethics in the context of education is a dynamic process that is influenced by the learner’s background and experiences, as well as the institutional context and the teacher’s approach to the subject.

(a) the teaching and learning process is a complex and dynamic process, (b) the process is shaped by a number of factors, (c) the teaching and research ethics in education is challenging, (d) the teaching and ethics are not easy to teach and to understand, (e) there is a need for a more comprehensive understanding of the ethical aspects of the teaching and learning processes, (f) the ethical aspects of teaching and learning are not well understood, (g) the
the threshold concept approach is useful for exploring the tensions in teaching research ethics to international postgraduates in education.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an ethical approach to the teaching of research ethics.
the question of how the internationalisation of the curriculum can be achieved in a context where there are conflicting expectations of what constitutes ethical research in education.
how we can teach and learn research ethics in education more inclusively and more ethically.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
research ethics in education is complex, and that the challenges of teaching and learning about it are significant.

the research ethics threshold concepts framework is a useful way of understanding how the teaching and learning relationship is mediated by the curriculum, and that it provides a way of thinking about research ethics that is not limited by disciplinary boundaries.

there is not a definitive way to teach research ethics, but rather that the teacher needs to engage with a variety of approaches to teaching research ethics in order to develop a critical understanding of research ethics and the role of the researcher in the research process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
research ethics in education is an important threshold concept that is difficult for students and staff to master.
we have been able to develop a research ethics module that is relevant and useful for students, and that is a valuable addition to the postgraduate curriculum in the UK.
we need to re-examine the way in which we teach and learn about research ethics in education.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we should avoid the temptation to assume that the same research ethics training is appropriate for all students and that we need to be more aware of the impact of our teaching on students from different cultures.
the teaching of research ethics in higher education is a political process and that the institutional and cultural context is a key determinant in the learning experience.
the teaching and learning experience of international postgraduate students can be enhanced by a more flexible approach to research ethics.
